messages:
Raj: Hey all — getting a surge of OAuth login failures from customers. Users start Google/GitHub SSO, go to provider, then back to our callback and we sometimes see: `state_mismatch` or occasionally `invalid_grant`. Roughly 8-12% of attempts fail. Callback URI configured: https://app.acme.example.com/auth/callback

Emma: Ugh. Thanks for the report. Quick checklist: 1) Which provider more often (Google or GitHub)? 2) Are you using PKCE? 3) Any CDN/reverse proxy in front (Cloudflare/nginx)? 4) Can you paste the browser error and the server log for the callback/token exchange? Also confirm redirect URI exact string in the provider consoles.

Raj: Both providers impacted but Google seems worse. Yes using PKCE (S256). We sit behind Cloudflare + nginx. Browser shows: "OAuth error: state did not match". Server callback log snippet when it fails:

```
2026-03-09T09:42:11Z ERROR auth callback: no state in session for code=4/XYZ987
stack: Error: PKCE verification failed
 at /srv/services/auth/callback.js:87:19
```

Mike: Two likely causes: 1) callback route doing a redirect that strips query params (trailing slash normalization etc), or 2) session cookie not present on return (SameSite or domain/path mismatch). With Cloudflare in the mix both are suspects.

Raj: We reproduced locally. Sometimes the provider hits /auth/callback?code=...&state=... then our app replies with a 301 -> /auth/callback/ and the Location header lacks the querystring. Screenshot of network trace: https://acme.screenshots/ss-oidc-301.png

Olivia: Bingo. If your server responds with a redirect that does not include `?`+$args, the state/code get dropped. Solutions: (A) ensure the provider redirect hits an exact no-redirect path (don't normalize slashes there), or (B) make your proxy/nginx preserve query string on rewrites. Example nginx approach to preserve args:

```
location = /auth/callback {
  proxy_pass http://auth-backend/auth/callback$is_args$args;
}
# If you rewrite, include ?$args:
rewrite ^/auth/callback$ /auth/callback/ permanent; # BAD -> loses args
rewrite ^/auth/callback$ /auth/callback/ permanent; # use /auth/callback/?$args to keep them
```

Olivia: Also verify cookie SameSite. If session cookie is `SameSite=Lax` it can be suppressed depending on provider redirect mechanics. For OAuth flows, set `SameSite=None; Secure` on the session cookie. Also confirm cookie domain/path and that Cloudflare isn't altering cookies.

Mike: Another check — ensure your trailing-slash middleware doesn't issue 302s for GETs to the exact callback path. A 302 that strips `req.url` querystring will cause state loss. Grep your middleware for redirects on "/auth/callback".

Raj: We have a central middleware that normalizes trailing slash. It issues a 301 canonical redirect for many routes. Looks like that behavior applies to /auth/callback and is indeed dropping the querystring. We can quick-patch the middleware to skip that path.

Leo: From security POV, if you saw tokens in logs or external endpoints, rotate client secret. But from these symptoms it looks like session/state loss instead of a leak.

Sam: Can you give exact repro steps we can run in staging? We'll add to the regression tests once we fix.

Raj: Repro steps we used:
1) Clear cookies for app.acme.example.com
2) Open incognito
3) Visit https://app.acme.example.com/login -> click Sign in with Google
4) Finish consent, provider redirects to https://app.acme.example.com/auth/callback?code=...&state=...
5) App responds 301 to /auth/callback/ and Location header does not include ?code&state -> callback fails and user sees an error page

Emma: For a quick server-side check, curl the URL and inspect Location header to see if query is preserved:

```
curl -v "https://app.acme.example.com/auth/callback?code=AAA&state=BBB"
# Look for 'Location:' header in the response; should include ?code=AAA&state=BBB if redirecting
```

Mike: We'll push two small changes: 1) update nginx config to ensure rewrites/passes preserve `$args`, and 2) update trailing-slash middleware to not redirect the callback path. Patch PR (internal): https://redwood.example.com/r/acme/oauth-trailing-slash-fix (WIP)

DeployBot: Deploy queued for branch acme/oauth-trailing-slash-fix — env: staging — ETA 2026-03-09T10:15:00Z

Raj: After we applied a config change to preserve args and disabled the redirect for /auth/callback, the failures disappeared for affected users. Monitoring shows error rate dropped to ~0% over past 90 minutes.

Olivia: Follow-ups: 1) Add an automated test that simulates provider redirect with query params and ensures the app doesn't drop them. 2) Add guidance to KB: common OAuth callback problems (trailing slash redirects, SameSite cookie, CDN/querystring stripping). Emma, can you create that KB and link it here?

Emma: Will do. I'll add the KB entry and include sample nginx snippets and curl checks. Will link here when done.

Sam: Also update the onboarding docs to tell customers: exact match of redirect URI matters (including trailing-slash variants) and session cookies should be `SameSite=None; Secure` for cross-site auth flows.

Leo: No immediate secret rotation required but if any customer reports weird token exposure escalate to Security.

Emma: Closing thread once KB published. :thumbsup:
